collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager gave a friend a favorite bowl and now misses it: ask to borrow it, or carve another one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A month ago, in a burst of generosity, (subject) gave (friend) (subject.his/her) favorite carved bowl. (friend) loves it and uses it every day. And every day (subject) sees it and misses it terribly, and wishes, just a little, that (subject.he/she) hadn't been quite so generous.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks, very casually, whether (subject.he/she) might borrow the bowl "just for one evening." (friend) hands it over gladly. (subject) eats (subject.his/her) dinner from it, perfectly happy, and gives it back. It becomes a habit: the bowl spends one evening a week at (subject)'s hut. (friend) doesn't mind at all.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) decides to carve (subject.him/her)self a bowl just like it. It takes weeks, and it isn't quite the same. But when (friend) sees it, (friend.he/she) says, "Oh, now we match!" That turns out to be nicer than having the original. Mostly.
